written_by: animation module (2026-10-31); read by the figures module. This file is the agreement on prop proportions; skeleton.json (src/figures3d/skeleton.mjs) is FIGURES' file and is not edited from here.
why: ANIM3D-NOTES section 8 request 1: the long_arm_sockets of skeleton.json put the lock nipple at 0.78 m, the small of the stock at 0.86 m and the fore end at 1.15 m from the butt of a 1.40 m arm. A rifle-musket's wrist (small of the stock, where the right hand grips) is about 0.30 m from the butt toe, the lock about 0.46 m, the lower band about 0.85 m. The hands of every animation clip are solved onto the numbers below (src/anim3d/figure-pose.mjs PROPS.rifle), so the mesh must use them or the hands will not meet the stock.
units: metres along the prop's +y axis from its origin (the butt toe for the rifle); prop frame = prop_long bone frame of skeleton.json
basis: kit/weapons.json m1861_springfield: overall length 56 in (1.422 m), barrel 40 in (1.016 m). Positions along the stock are inferred from those two printed lengths and the usual layout of a rifle-musket; they are not measured on a museum piece (no measured drawing was acquired). Registered as G-ANIM-13.

right_hand_ready_aim_fire.note: right hand at the wrist, thumb on the cock

left_hand_ready_aim_fire.note: left hand under the fore end between the guard and the lower band (the clips use 0.55 to 0.85)

carbine_left_hand.note: a cavalry carbine is shorter (about 0.99 m overall); the rider clips grip the forestock at 0.62

map_to_skeleton_long_arm_sockets.action: added by FIGURES: the left-hand grip point (the old fore_end 1.15 is the upper band)
the ramrod head sits 12 cm short of the muzzle when stowed
FIGURES now has 1.879 (socket bayonet); no clip uses the tip

prop_pole.uses: ramrod (origin at its head, +y toward the small end, 0.96 m), sponge-and-rammer staff (2.0 m), shovel, axe, rail, flag staff, ladle

prop_long_as_stretcher.handles: four corners; the front pair grips at 1.95 m along the prop, the rear pair at 0.15 m

prop_sword.note: the paired sabre clips put the blade point 0.55 m from the hilt on the contact point of the two figures

prop_instr.uses: bugle, drum, round of ammunition, cup, bucket

hand_socket_offsets_used.note: from skeleton.json sockets (the palm centre); unchanged

joint_limits: No change to the limits of skeleton.json is requested: the clips were re-authored and added a limited arm solve so that every clip stays inside them (0 frames with excess). Limits that FIGURES may wish to review with a source: the shoulder (upperarm z -20 degrees of adduction, y +-90 twist), which makes crossing the chest with a hand impossible without the elbow bent; widening them is optional and is not needed by the clips.
status: AGREED AND APPLIED: when this file was last checked (2026-10-31) the long_arm_sockets of skeleton.json already carried the agreed numbers (written by the figures module). tests/anim3d.test.mjs fails if skeleton.json and this file drift apart by more than 3 cm.

reins.written_by: figures module, round 3 (2026-10-31); read by the animation module. The rest of this file is ANIMATION's; src/figures3d/horse.mjs REIN_HAND and skeleton.mjs rein_hand_* follow this section (a test compares them).
reins.why: Round 2 left the rider's hands 19 cm from the rein sockets (the horse sockets rein_hand_L/R were at world (+-0.04, 1.66, 0.65); the baked rider_walk left palm socket sits at (0.153, 1.666, 0.443) and the right at (-0.120, 1.640, 0.380)). The sockets are now at the measured palm position and the rein mesh passes through the closed fist.
reins.frame: horse frame at rest (metres): x = the horse's left, y up, z forward; rider root = saddle_seat = spine2 + (0, 0.10, -0.06) = (0, 1.54, 0.04)
reins.hold: BRIDLE HAND: both reins in the rider's LEFT hand, the right hand free for the sabre or carbine (plausible-procedural: no cavalry manual was read for this task; gap G-FIG-REIN-HAND). The right rein runs from the right bit ring over the crest to the left hand.

rein_hand_L.role: target of the LEFT palm socket (grip_L) of every mounted clip with a bridle hand

rein_hand_R.role: target of the RIGHT palm socket for two-handed riders (horse-artillery mounted cannoneers, hart_* clips); the cavalry rein mesh ends at the LEFT hand only

reins.rein_path_passes_through: fist_centre_m (measured on the hand mesh of rider_walk at grip 0.92; the reins are 3.2 mm radius leather tubes: bit ring, over a sag, through the fist, then a 0.2 m tail toward the near side of the pommel)
request_to_animation: Set gripL to 0.9 or more in every mounted clip while the bridle hand holds the reins (rider_walk has 0.22: the fingers do not close on the rein).

Solve grip_L onto rein_hand_L (tolerance 1 cm) for rider_walk, rider_sabre_carry and the other cavalry clips; the rein_hand_L socket is a spring bone child of the head, so the hand follows the head nod.

Two-handed riders: grip_L on rein_hand_L and grip_R on rein_hand_R; the right rein of the mesh then runs to the left fist (a second rein mesh variant horse:riding2 can be added if the clip needs the right rein in the right hand).
Right hand with a weapon at (-0.12, 1.64, 0.38): keep.

crew_stations.written_by: figures module, round 3 (2026-10-31); read by the animation module. Positions are the drill tables' (src/anim3d/drill-tables.mjs crewPosts, drill items ART-FA-02..04: gunner at the end of the trail handspike, Nos. 1 and 2 about two feet outside the wheels abreast the front of the wheel, Nos. 3 and 4 in line with the knob of the cascable covering them), in the piece frame: +z toward the muzzle, +x the piece's LEFT, origin on the axle line.
crew_stations.finding: The clips' workPos for Nos. 3 and 4 (x +-0.45, z -0.45) lies INSIDE the wheel track (half 0.78) and inside the wheel diameter (z -0.73..+0.73): a man standing there is between the wheel and the trail, not beside the breech as the drill has him (outside the wheel, then stepping in behind it). Nos. 1 and 2 at (+-0.45, 1.45) stand in front of the wheel beside the muzzle, which agrees with "steps to opposite the muzzle". The contact sheets show the detachment at the drill posts (gun_crew_napoleon.png) and at the clips' working places (gun_crew_working.png).
request_to_animation: Re-base the working places of Nos. 3 and 4 to z -1.0 .. -1.15 at x +-0.9 (behind the wheel, reaching the vent over the trail) or document why the clip stands inside the wheel; keep the posts of the table as the idle places.
